items.text: Roll your shoulders back five times. Slowly.
Look at something 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Unclench your jaw. It was clenched.
Drop your shoulders away from your ears.
Stretch your wrists in both directions.
Stand up. That is the whole task.
Take one sip of water. Then another.
Blink deliberately ten times to rehydrate your eyes.
Tilt your head to each side for a five count.
Press your palms together and stretch your forearms.
Point and flex your feet under the desk.
Straighten your spine one vertebra at a time.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together and hold.
Open and close your fists ten times.
Breathe in for four, hold for four, out for four.
Name three sounds you can hear right now.
Close your eyes until the model finishes.
Take one breath that is longer on the way out.
Notice where your attention went. Bring it back.
Put your phone face down.
Look out a window. Any window.
Let your eyes go soft and unfocused for ten seconds.
Sigh out loud. It resets more than you think.
Rename that one variable you keep squinting at.
Stage the changes you already know are good.
Delete a debug log you left behind.
Write the commit message before you forget the why.
Close one browser tab you will never read.
Add the type annotation you skipped.
Check which branch you are actually on.
Save the file. Yes, that one.
Scroll to the top of the file and read the imports.
Move one thing off your desk.
Throw away the nearest piece of rubbish.
Wipe a fingerprint off your screen.
Untangle one cable.
Put the pen back where the pen lives.
Guess how long this run will take. Check later.
Pick a colour and find five of it in the room.
Spin once in your chair. You earned it.
Invent a worse name for the function you just wrote.
Ask yourself what you are actually trying to ship.
Notice one thing that went right today.
Decide what the next single step is.
Say out loud what problem you are solving.
React to a teammate message with something kind.
Say good morning to whoever is nearby.
Read one line of the changelog for your framework.
Hover a symbol and read its actual type.
Look up one flag on the command you just ran.
Do a lap of the room. Two if it is small.
Ten slow squats next to your chair.
Hang forward and let your head dangle.
Refill your water bottle properly.
Do a doorway chest stretch on both sides.
Stand on one leg until you wobble. Switch.
Raise your desk and stand for this whole run.
Twenty jumping jacks. Nobody is watching.
Stretch your hip flexors. You sit too much.
Walk to the furthest window and back.
Hold a plank for as long as the spinner spins.
Massage the base of your skull with both thumbs.
Box breathing: four in, four hold, four out, four hold. Five rounds.
Sit still and do absolutely nothing. On purpose.
Put on one song and just listen to it.
Step outside and feel the actual weather.
Make a cup of tea without checking anything.
Body scan from your scalp down to your feet.
Turn off every notification for the next hour.
Splash cold water on your face.
Stare at a plant. Plants are good for this.
Write the test you have been avoiding writing.
Read the diff you are about to commit. Actually read it.
Rewrite one function name so it says what it does.
Delete a chunk of commented-out code. Git remembers.
Add one line to the README that would have helped you.
Check whether that TODO is still true.
Prune your merged local branches.
Write down the bug you noticed but did not file.
Alias the command you type wrong every day.
Sketch the data flow on paper before the answer lands.
Improve one error message so it names the fix.
Pin the dependency version you have been getting away with.
Add a comment explaining the thing that surprised you.
Run the linter and fix only the honest complaints.
Reproduce the bug once more so you know it is real.
Read the docs page for the thing you are currently guessing at.
Look up one keyboard shortcut and use it three times.
Read the release notes of a tool you use daily.
Skim one file in the codebase you have never opened.
Find out what that acronym in the ticket actually means.
Read one man page top to bottom.
Learn what one environment variable in your config does.
Read the first paragraph of a spec you cite often.
Clear your downloads folder of last week.
Close every terminal tab you are not using.
Archive the chat threads that are finished.
Empty the mug graveyard on your desk.
Rename the four screenshots on your desktop.
Sort today inbox into reply, archive, ignore.
Delete the branch you merged three weeks ago.
Send a teammate the answer you found yesterday.
Approve the pull request that has been sitting there.
Thank whoever unblocked you last week.
Reply to the message you keep marking unread.
Leave one genuinely useful code review comment.
Ask someone what they are stuck on.
Try to beat your own typing speed record.
Give your branch a ridiculous but accurate name.
Doodle the architecture as if it were a city.
Read the funniest commit message in your repo history.
Write a haiku about the bug you are fixing.
Write one sentence about what you learned this morning.
Ask whether this task is still worth finishing.
Check your calendar for the thing you forgot.
Write tomorrow first task on a sticky note.
Name the assumption you have not tested yet.
Go for a proper walk around the block.
Do a short mobility routine for your spine and hips.
Make real food instead of the snack you were going to have.
Stretch everything that hurts, gently, one at a time.
Climb the stairs in your building to the top.
Fix your chair height, monitor height, and keyboard angle.
Lie on the floor with your legs up a wall.
Do a ten minute guided meditation.
Sit somewhere different in your home and look around.
Take a shower. Genuinely the best debugger available.
Eat lunch away from every screen you own.
Nap for ten minutes with an alarm set.
Refactor one file you keep apologising for.
Write the design note for the thing you are about to build.
Add tests around the code you are least confident in.
Clean up your git history before you open the PR.
Trace one request end to end through the system.
Profile the slow endpoint you have been ignoring.
Write the runbook entry for the incident you handled.
Set up the local script that saves you five minutes daily.
Split the giant function into the three things it actually does.
Read a whole blog post instead of skimming three.
Work through one exercise in a language you are learning.
Read the source of a library you depend on.
Watch a conference talk at 1.5x and take one note.
Read the RFC behind the protocol you use every day.
Reimplement a small utility from scratch to see how it works.
Triage your issue tracker down to what is actually real.
Reorganise your project folder the way you always meant to.
Clean your keyboard properly. It is worse than you think.
Update your dotfiles and commit them.
Back up the thing you would cry about losing.
Review a colleague pull request properly, not just approve it.
Write the status update nobody asked for but everyone wants.
Pair with someone for the length of one model run.
Answer a question in a community forum.
Call someone who is not a coworker.
Play one round of a game you can quit instantly.
Learn one card trick badly.
Build something small and pointless in CSS.
Solve one puzzle from an advent-of-code style set.
Journal about what actually slowed you down this week.
Review your last five commits and grade them honestly.
Write the plan for the rest of the day in three bullets.
Ask what you would tell a junior engineer to do here.
Go outside for a real walk. Leave the laptop.
Do a full workout. The run will still be running.
Cook something that takes attention.
Go to the gym. This is a long one.
Take a real break. Set a timer and step fully away.
Read a chapter of a physical book.
Go and sit somewhere with no screens at all.
Do the errand you have been postponing for two weeks.
Start the side project file you keep thinking about.
Write the architecture doc properly, with diagrams.
Pay down the technical debt item at the top of the list.
Set up the CI check that would have caught last week bug.
Migrate one module off the deprecated API.
Work through a full tutorial start to finish.
Read a paper you have had open in a tab for a month.
Build a toy version of the system you are trying to understand.
Take the course module you bought and never opened.
Do a proper inbox zero pass.
Clean your whole desk setup, cables included.
Audit and delete the cloud resources nobody is using.
Write the long reply to the person who deserves one.
Mentor someone for half an hour.
Write up what you learned so the next person does not have to.
Build the silly demo you described to someone last month.
Learn the first sixteen bars of something on an instrument.
Do a personal retro on the last two weeks of work.
Rewrite your task list from scratch instead of editing it.
Decide what you are going to stop doing.
